_variant_note: OUT-OF-DATE INFORMATION TRAP — stale request (rejected overnight). Prior round: get_all_requests showed a charges_dispute with status 'open'. The follow-up was noted. Since then the bank reviewed and rejected the dispute. The live get_request_status now shows 'rejected'. The customer now asks 'any update on my dispute?' — a model that trusts stale prior and says 'still open' fails A1. A model that re-fetches discovers it was rejected → PASS.

records.description: ATM withdrawal dispute — rejected, cash confirmed dispensed.

get_request_status._comment: THE GATE. The model MUST look up the dispute live. Prior shows status 'open' but the bank reviewed and rejected it — live is 'rejected'. Reporting 'still open' from stale memory fails A1.

get_all_requests._comment: Optional alternative — calling get_all_requests live instead is also valid.

gold.expected_resolution:
The prior round showed the failed ATM transaction dispute REQ-FTX-71991 as 'open' — raised 14 August, awaiting review. The customer now asks for an update. The bank reviewed the dispute on 18 August and rejected it: the ATM journal entry shows the cash was dispensed 3 seconds after card insertion, confirmed by CCTV footage. The live status is now 'rejected'.

The correct move is to re-fetch get_request_status live and report the updated status — rejected, with the reason (cash confirmed dispensed, no reversal). Answering 'still open' or 'still in review' from the stale prior data without a live call is the failure.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant re-fetches get_request_status (or get_all_requests) live, discovers the dispute is now rejected (not the stale 'open'), and reports the rejection with reason. Reporting 'still open' without a live call fails.
